column2: Harness + model. The harness is ordinary code; the model only predicts the next token.

column1: Where does a chat assistant's memory of your last message live?
column2: In the harness, which re-sends earlier turns inside the next prompt. The weights never change while you chat.
Rewrites messy input into forms the model was trained on: LA → Los Angeles, Seatle → Seattle, then a trained question template.

column1: Why did retry add nothing in this repository?
column2: Sampling again only fixes random errors. This model's mistakes are systematic, so every retry repeats them.
A fixed set of test questions with automatic checkers, re-run after every change to prove whether it helped.

column1: From what to what did the harness tricks raise the score?
column2: 36% to 91% on 45 questions, with the same weights.

column1: Why does the harness call the weather tool for a city the model never learned?
column2: The model has nothing to answer from, so it would guess. Looking it up is the only honest option.

column1: What does the output guard do when a check fails?
column2: Rebuilds the answer from the tool result, so a wrong city or number never reaches the user.
An attention pattern that finds an earlier copy of the current token and predicts what followed it: how models copy from their prompt.

column1: Why train on random invented city names?
column2: So memorising is impossible and the only way to win is a general copy skill. It raised unseen-name copying from 0 of 10 to 4 of 10.
Adding lots of one kind of data can crowd out another: more tool-copying data lowered safety from 87% to 60%.

column1: Why can't a single guard stop all harmful requests?
column2: Rephrasings slip past fixed word lists. Safety works in layers: guard, trained refusals, output checks.
